p.d: Input polyline layer (3D vertices; 2D vertices are handled as a planar special case).
Optional output path. If omitted, the result is stored in memory.
Maximum 3D deviation in map units. Vertices closer than this to the chord are removed.
Multiplier applied to Z before the distance test, for data whose Z unit differs from XY (default 1).

s: Extrudes 3D solids along the solar vector to the ground to produce closed shadow-volume solids for a given date and time (ArcGIS Sun Shadow Volume). shadow_image, shadow_animation and time_in_daylight all work on a raster DSM and emit rasters, and solar_radiation computes irradiance — none produces shadow geometry, so questions like 'is this window shaded' or 'how much of this plot's airspace is in shadow' cannot be answered. The output composes with inside_3d, intersect_3d and union_3d.

p.d: 3D building solids or extruded footprints (triangle-mesh MultiPolygons with Z).
Closed shadow-volume solids. If omitted, stored in memory.
Local date-time of the sun position as 'YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM' or 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM'. Taken as a parameter, never from a clock, so results are reproducible.
Latitude in degrees, used for the solar geometry. Required: it cannot be derived without a projection engine.
Hours from UTC of the supplied local time (default 0).
Treat the supplied time as daylight-saving-adjusted, subtracting an hour before the solar calculation (default false), matching ArcGIS.
Constant ground Z the shadow is projected onto. Default: each feature's own minimum Z.
Cap on the sweep distance in CRS units, so a low sun does not produce a kilometres-long prism. Default: unlimited.

s: Computes the combined volume of overlapping closed 3D solids without double-counting their intersections, plus per-pair overlap volumes (ArcGIS Union 3D). Neither registry has any 3D overlay, so summing buffer_3d capsules or minimum_bounding_volume hulls today double-counts every overlap; polygon_volume and surface_volume only measure against a reference plane. Per-solid volumes are exact (signed-tetrahedron summation); the union is estimated by voxel occupancy at a reported resolution.

p.d: Closed 3D solid features (triangle-mesh MultiPolygons with Z, as buffer_3d and minimum_bounding_volume emit).
Optional output table path of per-group volumes. If omitted, stored in memory.
Optional field; solids are unioned within each group value rather than across the whole layer.
Optional path for the per-pair overlap volumes. If omitted, stored in memory (still returned).
Voxel samples per axis used to estimate the union volume, 4 to 512 (default 96). Higher is more accurate and slower.

s: Extracts a triangulated isosurface at one or more threshold values from a 3D voxel field via marching tetrahedra (ArcGIS Export Voxel Isosurface). The whole contouring suite in both registries is 2D — lines from a plane; this is the volumetric analogue, turning the output of idw_3d or a multidimensional raster into renderable geometry. Emits the triangle-mesh convention used by buffer_3d and minimum_bounding_volume, so results feed straight into inside_3d.

p.d: Voxel field as a multi-band raster: band k is the Z slice at z_min + k * z_spacing.
Threshold value(s): a number, a JSON array of numbers, or a comma-separated string. One surface per value.
Optional output path for the triangle-mesh surfaces. If omitted, stored in memory.
Z coordinate of the first slice (default 0).
Vertical spacing between slices (default 1).

Cap surfaces where they meet the volume edge so the result bounds a closed solid (default true). Implemented by marching an extra below-iso shell, so the cap is welded to the surface; it lies between the boundary plane and one cell beyond it. This seals the OUTER faces only: cells touching interior no-data are skipped, so a no-data pocket that intersects the extracted surface still leaves an open rim (one lying wholly inside or outside the contour never meets the mesh).
Laplacian smoothing iterations applied to the extracted mesh (default 0).

s: Adds a new attribute field with an optional default value.

p.d: Input vector layer.
New field name.
Field type: integer, float, text, boolean.
Optional default value.
Output vector path.

s: Automatically calculates geometric properties (area, length, perimeter, centroid) and adds them as new fields, supporting both planar and geodesic measurements.

p.d: Input vector layer.
Measurement method: auto (default), planar, or geodesic.
Include area field (AREA_M2 for geodesic, AREA_MAP2 for planar).
Include length field (LENGTH_M for geodesic, LENGTH_MAP for planar).
Include perimeter field (PERIM_M for geodesic, PERIM_MAP for planar).
Include centroid X/Y fields (default true).
Output vector path.

s: Performs Pearson correlation analysis on numeric vector attribute fields.

p.d: Input vector path.
Optional HTML report output path (alias: output_html_file).

s: Creates a histogram for numeric field values in a vector attribute table.

p.d: Input vector path.
Numeric attribute field name.
Optional HTML report output path (alias: output_html_file).

s: Computes scatterplot summary statistics between two numeric vector fields.

p.d: Input vector path.
Numeric x-axis field name.
Numeric y-axis field name.
Include trendline summary (default false).
Optional HTML report output path (alias: output_html_file).

s: Combine several numeric attributes into a composite index (like ArcGIS Calculate Composite Index): per-variable scaling (min-max/z-score/percentile) with optional reversal, weighted combination (mean/sum/geometric mean), and output rescaling — the vector-side sibling of fuzzy_overlay.

p.d: Input vector layer (or table) with numeric variable fields.
Comma-separated variable fields; append ':reverse' to a field whose high values should lower the index (e.g. 'income:reverse,unemployment').
Output vector layer with the index fields added. If omitted, stored in memory.
Per-variable scaling: 'minmax' (default), 'zscore', 'percentile', or 'none'.
Comma-separated weights matching 'fields' (default: equal weights).
How to combine scaled variables: 'mean' (default), 'sum', or 'geometric_mean'.
Rescale the combined index: 'minmax' (0–1, default), 'zero_to_100', 'zscore', or 'none'.

s: Deletes one or more attribute fields from a vector layer.

p.d: Input vector layer.
Comma-delimited field names to delete.
Output vector path.

s: Extracts vector features that satisfy an attribute expression.

p.d: Input vector layer.
Boolean expression evaluated against attribute fields; accepts SQL-style AND/OR/NOT/XOR aliases.
Output vector path.

s: Calculates a field value from an expression using feature attributes and geometry variables; supports SQL-style CASE, CAST, null checks, and UPDATE ... SET ... [WHERE ...] wrappers.

p.d: Input vector layer.
Output field name.
Output field type: float, integer, text.
Expression evaluated per feature. Supports SQL-style CASE, CAST(... AS type), IS NULL/IS NOT NULL, and UPDATE ... SET FIELD = ... [WHERE ...] wrappers.
Overwrite existing field if present (default true).
Optional number of preview rows to return in the result payload. When > 0, output may be omitted for preview-only evaluation.
Output vector path. Optional when preview_rows > 0.

s: Filters polygon features below a minimum area threshold.

p.d: Input polygon vector layer.
Minimum polygon area to retain, in layer coordinate units squared.
Output vector path.

s: Find features that are identical on geometry and/or chosen fields, grouping duplicates; 'report' adds dup_group/dup_seq columns, 'delete' keeps only the first of each group, like ArcGIS Find Identical / Delete Identical.

p.d: Input vector layer to deduplicate.
Output vector path (driver from extension). If omitted, stored in memory.
Comma-separated fields to compare. Omit to compare geometry only; combine with 'compare_geometry'.
Whether geometry is part of the identity test (default true; set false to compare fields only).
Snap tolerance for geometry comparison (vertices are rounded to this grid before hashing). Default 0 (exact).
'report' (default; adds dup_group/dup_seq) or 'delete' (keeps the first of each group).

s: Lists unique values and frequencies in a vector attribute field.

p.d: Input vector path.
Attribute field name.
Optional output CSV path.

s: Derive criterion weights from an AHP pairwise-comparison matrix (Saaty 1-9 scale) as the normalized principal eigenvector, with a consistency check (lambda_max, consistency index, consistency ratio) — like ArcGIS Assign Weights By Pairwise Comparison.

p.d: The n x n reciprocal comparison matrix as a JSON 2-D array, e.g. [[1,3,5],[0.333,1,2],[0.2,0.5,1]]. Provide this or `input`.
CSV file holding the comparison matrix (plain numeric rows, or labeled with a header row and a leading name column). Provide this or `matrix`.
Comma-separated criterion names (must match the matrix order). Overrides CSV labels; defaults to C1..Cn.
Output table path — a CSV (extension .csv) or a geometry-less vector table (criterion, weight, rank). If omitted, stored in memory.

s: Reshape a long-form attribute table to wide: one output row per unique combination of the identity fields, and one column per distinct value of the pivot field, filled from the value field. Like ArcGIS Pivot Table.

p.d: Input vector layer or attribute table in long form.
Output table path (driver from extension). If omitted, stored in memory.
Comma/semicolon-separated field name(s) identifying an output row; carried through unchanged.
Field whose distinct values become new columns.
Field supplying the cell values.
Applied when one row/column cell has multiple source records: 'first' (default), 'sum', 'mean', 'min', 'max', 'count'.

s: Classify a numeric vector attribute into class bins (like ArcGIS Reclassify Field): equal_interval, defined_interval, quantile, natural_breaks (Jenks), std_dev, or geometric_interval, writing an integer class field plus an optional break-value field.

p.d: Input vector layer (or table) with the numeric field to classify.
Name of the numeric field to classify.
Output vector layer with the class field added. If omitted, stored in memory.
Classification method: equal_interval, defined_interval, quantile, natural_breaks, std_dev, or geometric_interval (default natural_breaks).
Number of classes for equal_interval/quantile/natural_breaks/geometric_interval (default 5). Ignored by defined_interval and std_dev, whose class count follows the data.
Fixed class width for defined_interval (required for that method).
Interval size for std_dev, in units of standard deviation (default 1.0; e.g. 0.5 for half-sigma bands).
Name of the integer class field to add (default 'class').
If given, also add a float field with the upper class limit each feature falls under.

s: Renames an attribute field in a vector layer.

p.d: Input vector layer.
Existing field name.
Replacement field name.
Output vector path.

s: Reorder a vector layer by attribute fields or along a Hilbert space-filling curve (spatial sort), like ArcGIS Sort — Hilbert ordering clusters spatially-near records to improve GeoParquet pruning and PMTiles locality.

p.d: Input vector layer.
Output vector layer in the new order. If omitted, stored in memory.
'hilbert' (spatial curve order; default) or 'attribute' (by the 'fields' list).
attribute mode: comma-separated fields with optional direction, e.g. 'pop:desc,name:asc'.
Optional field name to store each feature's Hilbert-curve distance.

s: Randomly split a feature layer into a training subset and its complement (test subset), by percentage or absolute count, using a seeded deterministic RNG. Optionally stratified by a group field. Like ArcGIS Subset Features.

p.d: Input vector layer (any geometry type).
Output path for the training subset. If omitted, stored in memory.
Optional output path for the complement (test) subset. If omitted, the test subset is stored in memory.
Training subset size: a percentage (0-100) or an absolute feature count, per 'size_method' (default 50).
'percentage' (default) or 'absolute'.
RNG seed for a reproducible split (default fixed constant).
Optional field to stratify on: each group contributes its own proportional share of the training subset.

s: SQL-style GROUP BY over one or more case fields: for each unique case-field combination, compute a list of (field, statistic) aggregates (count/sum/mean/min/max/std/first/last) plus a group record count. Output is a pure attribute table. No case field yields a single grand-total row (like ArcGIS's Summary Statistics; count-only reproduces Frequency).

p.d: Input vector layer or attribute table to aggregate.
Semicolon/comma-separated list of 'field statistic' pairs (also accepts 'field:statistic'), e.g. 'population sum; population mean; elev max'. Statistics: count, sum, mean, min, max, std, first, last.
Optional comma/semicolon-separated case (GROUP BY) field name(s). If omitted, a single summary row is produced over the whole table.

Optional output table path (driver from its extension; GeoParquet or CSV). If omitted, the table is stored in memory. Columns: the case fields, a record 'count', then one '<field>_<statistic>' column per requested pair.

s: Standardize, transform, and encode attribute fields (like ArcGIS Standardize/Transform/Encode Field): z-score, min-max, robust, log/log1p/sqrt/boxcox/inverse, equal-interval/quantile/std-dev binning, and one-hot encoding.

p.d: Input vector layer (or table) with the fields to transform.
Comma-separated field names to transform; the same transform is applied to each.
Transform to apply: zscore, minmax, robust, log, log1p, sqrt, boxcox, inverse, bin, onehot.
Output vector layer with the transformed fields added. If omitted, stored in memory.
Number of classes for 'bin' (default 5).
Classification method for 'bin': equal_interval (default), quantile, or std_dev.
Fixed lambda for 'boxcox'; if omitted, fit by maximum likelihood (golden-section search).
Output field name suffix (default depends on transform, e.g. '_z' for zscore).
If true, remove the original field(s) from the output after transforming (default false).

s: Reshapes a wide attribute table to long form: each listed value column becomes its own row, tagged with the column it came from (ArcGIS Transpose Fields). pivot_table only goes long-to-wide, so tables arriving with one column per period could not be fed to the time-series tools that need one row per observation.

p.d: Input vector layer or table.
Comma- or semicolon-separated value columns to unpivot.
Name of the output column holding the cell value (default 'VALUE').
Name of the output column holding the source column name (default 'FIELD').
Optional labels written into 'transposed_field' instead of the raw column names, e.g. '2000,2010,2020'. Must have the same length as 'transpose_fields'.
Attributes copied onto every output row. Defaults to all non-transposed fields.
Skip output rows whose value is null (default false).
Output layer. If omitted, stored in memory.

s: Group points that fall within an aggregation distance of each other into cluster polygons (convex hull or buffered union), each carrying a point count and optional per-cluster field sums, like ArcGIS Aggregate Points.

p.d: Input point vector layer (Point or MultiPoint).
Output polygon vector path (driver from extension). If omitted, stored in memory.
Maximum distance between points for them to join the same cluster (map units).
Minimum points a cluster needs to be output (default 2; set 1 to keep singletons).
'convex_hull' (default) or 'buffer' (buffered union eroded back).
Comma-separated numeric fields to sum per cluster (output columns 'sum_<field>').

s: Combine polygons within an aggregation distance into larger polygons (morphological closing), with minimum-area and minimum-hole-size filters and an optional barrier layer aggregation may not cross.

p.d: Input polygon vector layer, format auto-detected (or in-memory handle).
Optional output vector path (driver from its extension). If omitted, stored in memory.
Polygons within this distance (CRS units) of each other are aggregated. Sets the morphological-closing radius to half this value.
Drop aggregated polygons whose area (CRS units squared) is below this value. Default: keep all.
Fill interior holes whose area (CRS units squared) is below this value. Default: keep all holes.
Optional barrier vector layer (lines or polygons) that aggregation may not cross; bridges spanning a barrier are severed. Existing input polygons are never split.

s: Populate eight directional neighbour-sheet fields (N, NE, E, SE, S, SW, W, NW) on each tile of a map-series index grid with the adjoining page's name, for 'continued on sheet …' margin labels — like ArcGIS Calculate Adjacent Fields.

p.d: Input polygon map-series index grid (e.g. output of grid_index_features).
Field whose value labels each page (written into the neighbours' directional fields).
Output polygon vector (driver from extension). If omitted, stored in memory.
Also populate the four diagonal fields (NE, SE, SW, NW) from corner-touching tiles. Default true.
Quantize vertices onto a grid of this size (CRS units) before matching borders. Default 0 (exact coordinates).

s: Compute a per-feature central meridian and two standard parallels from each feature's extent, for map-series and atlas pages, like ArcGIS Calculate Central Meridian And Parallels.

p.d: Input features in geographic coordinates (longitude/latitude), typically a grid_index_features page grid.
Optional output path. If omitted, the result is stored in memory.
Name of the central-meridian field to write (default 'central_meridian').
Fraction of the latitude range used to inset each standard parallel from the feature's edge (default 0.1667, Esri's 1/6 rule). Must be in [0, 0.5).

s: Distort polygons so area is proportional to an attribute value: non-contiguous (scale each polygon about its centroid) or Dorling (proportional circles with overlap removal).

p.d: Input polygon vector layer, format auto-detected (or in-memory handle).
Optional output vector path (driver from its extension). If omitted, stored in memory.
Numeric field whose value each feature's area should be proportional to.
'non_contiguous' (default; scale polygons in place) or 'dorling' (proportional circles).
Dorling overlap-removal iterations (default 100). Ignored by non_contiguous.

s: Detect pairs of roughly parallel lines within a width tolerance (dual carriageways, road casings) and replace each pair with a single centerline, reconnecting junctions — like ArcGIS Collapse Dual Lines To Centerline.

p.d: Input line vector layer (projected CRS; widths in its units).
Output line vector path (driver from extension). If omitted, stored in memory.
Minimum separation between paired lines, in CRS units (default 0).
Maximum separation between paired lines, in CRS units. Required (the collapse width).
Optional field that must match for two lines to pair (e.g. road name or class).
Densification interval for parallelism testing, in CRS units. Default: max_width / 2.
Minimum fraction of a line that must run parallel to its partner to pair (0-1, default 0.5).

s: Collapse narrow water polygons to centerlines while keeping wide reaches as polygons (like ArcGIS Collapse Hydro Polygon): trace each polygon's centerline along its principal axis via perpendicular cross-section midpoints, measure local width, and collapse where the median width is at or below a threshold. The width-thresholded polygon→line generalization the line-casing collapse_dual_lines_to_centerline and raster river_centerlines don't do.

p.d: Input water polygon layer.
Output centerline layer for collapsed (narrow) polygons. If omitted, stored in memory.
Polygons whose median width is at or below this collapse to a centerline.
Spacing of cross-section stations along the axis (default: collapse_width / 2).
Drop collapsed centerlines shorter than this (default 0).
Optional output polygon layer for wide (non-collapsed) reaches.

s: Collapse small road loops and jogs (roundabouts, dogbones, offset jogs) below a diameter threshold to single through-connections for small-scale display, preserving network connectivity — like ArcGIS Collapse Road Detail.

p.d: Input road (line) vector layer, format auto-detected (or in-memory handle).
Optional output vector path (driver from its extension). If omitted, stored in memory.
Maximum detail diameter to collapse. Loops/jogs whose bounding diameter is below this (metres for a geographic CRS, CRS units otherwise) are collapsed; larger ones are kept.
Optional road-class field. When set, only loops whose boundary roads all share the same class value are collapsed (junctions between different classes are preserved).
Distance within which road endpoints are treated as the same junction. Default 1e-6.

s: Assign each polygon a small integer colour index so no two adjacent polygons share a value (like ArcGIS Calculate Color Theorem Field) — adjacency-safe choropleth styling via DSATUR graph colouring over shared-edge (or shared-corner) contiguity.

p.d: Input polygon layer.
Output polygon layer with the colour field added. If omitted, stored in memory.
Name of the colour index field to write (default 'color_id').
'edge' (rook, shared border; default) or 'edge_or_corner' (queen, shared border or vertex).
Grid size to snap vertices to before matching borders (default 0 = exact).

s: Density-equalizing (Gastner-Newman diffusion) cartogram: distorts polygon areas in proportion to an attribute while keeping the map a connected sheet with shared borders (ArcGIS Generate Contiguous Cartogram). The shipped cartogram tool implements only the non-contiguous and Dorling methods, both of which destroy adjacency, and its own module doc defers the contiguous form.

p.d: Contiguous polygon layer.
Positive numeric attribute whose total the areas should become proportional to.
Density grid resolution; must be a power of two (default 256). The dominant accuracy/cost knob.
Diffusion steps (default 20). More steps equalize density further at the cost of more distortion.
Gaussian pre-smoothing of the density field, in grid cells (default 0.5). Prevents the extreme distortion a hard density discontinuity produces.
Density outside the study area: 'mean' (default) or 'min'. This materially changes the result at the map edge.
Maximum edge segment length in grid cells before vertices are inserted (default 1.0). Long straight borders otherwise separate from their neighbours.
Output polygon layer with displaced vertices and the original attributes. If omitted, stored in memory.

s: Produce adaptive, non-overlapping partition polygons that each hold roughly a target feature count (denser where data clusters) so large generalization / masking jobs can be tiled coverage-safely — a pure-Rust counterpart of ArcGIS Create Cartographic Partitions.

p.d: Input vector layer (any geometry). Each feature is reduced to a representative point and assigned to one partition.
Target maximum number of features per partition. A cell is split while it still holds more than this many features. Default 1000.
Output polygon vector of partitions (driver from extension). If omitted, stored in memory.

s: Build knockout mask polygons (and optional wing-tick decoration lines) where an 'above' line crosses a 'below' line, so the lower line is masked at the crossing.

p.d: Line vector of features that pass OVER the crossing (the mask is oriented along these). Format auto-detected, or in-memory handle.
Line vector of features masked UNDER the crossing (the lines to be knocked out). Format auto-detected, or in-memory handle.
Optional output path for the mask polygons (driver from its extension). If omitted, stored in memory.
Optional output path for the wing-tick decoration lines. If omitted, stored in memory (still returned as 'output_decoration').
Half-length of each mask along the above line, in CRS units (mask length is 2x this). Default 1.0.
Half-width of each mask across the above line, in CRS units (mask width is 2x this). Default 1.0.
Decoration style: 'none', 'perpendicular' (default; a tick across each mask end) or 'parallel' (casing lines along each side).

s: At line crossings, builds mask polygons oriented along the upper feature and cuts a matching gap out of the lower feature so it reads as passing beneath (ArcGIS Create Underpass). Sibling of the shipped create_overpass, which masks the lower line so the upper one reads continuous; an underpass instead needs the decorative break, which is what distinguishes a tunnel portal from a bridge. Emits both the masks and the trimmed lower lines.

p.d: Line vector of features that pass OVER the crossing (masks are oriented along these). Format auto-detected, or in-memory handle.
Line vector of features that pass UNDER the crossing (the lines that get the gap). Format auto-detected, or in-memory handle.
Optional output path for the underpass mask polygons. If omitted, stored in memory.
Optional output path for the below layer with underpass gaps cut out. If omitted, stored in memory (still returned as 'output_lines').
Half-length of each mask measured ALONG the above line, in CRS units; the mask spans 2x this in that direction. Default 1.0.
Half-width of each mask ACROSS the above line, in CRS units. For a perpendicular crossing this is what bounds the gap cut into the below line, so the removed length is 2x this. Default 1.0.
Skip crossings where the two lines meet at less than this angle in degrees, since a near-parallel mask is unstable. Default 15.

s: Generate scale-aware knockout mask polygons at cul-de-sac bulbs in a road network, like ArcGIS Cul-De-Sac Masks.

p.d: Road centerline layer.
Optional output mask polygon path. If omitted, stored in memory.
Map scale denominator the mask is sized for (e.g. 24000 for 1:24,000).
Road casing width in page units (see 'page_unit') at the reference scale.
Extra margin around the symbol, in page units (default 0).
Unit of 'symbol_width' and 'margin': points (default, 1/72 inch), mm, or inches.
CRS units per metre (default 1, correct for metre-based projected CRSs). For a layer in degrees use about 0.000008983.
Coordinate snapping tolerance for joining line endpoints into network nodes (default 0.001 map units).
ids_only (default) | all — whether to carry the source feature's attributes onto the mask.

s: Generalize dense building footprints into smooth settlement / urban-extent polygons by grouping nearby buildings (morphological closing), with minimum building-count and area filters.

p.d: Input building-footprint polygon layer, format auto-detected (or in-memory handle).
Optional output vector path (driver from its extension). If omitted, stored in memory.
Buildings whose footprints lie within this distance (CRS units) are grouped into one built-up area. Sets the morphological-closing radius to half this value.
Drop built-up areas that contain fewer than this many buildings (default 1 — keep every group).
Drop built-up areas whose area (CRS units squared) is below this value, and fill interior holes smaller than it. Default: keep all.
Douglas–Peucker tolerance (CRS units) applied to the built-up boundary to thin the vertex-dense rounded buffer. Default 0 (no simplification).

s: Find where the symbolized (drawn-width) extents of two feature layers — or one layer against itself — overlap or crowd within a minimum separation, emitting a conflict polygon per conflicting pair tagged with both source feature ids and the overlap area, like ArcGIS Detect Graphic Conflict.

p.d: Input vector layer (points, lines, or polygons).
Second vector layer to check 'input' against. Omit to check 'input' against itself.
Symbolized width/diameter of 'input' features, in map units.
Symbolized width/diameter of 'conflict' features, in map units. Default: same as 'symbol_width'. Ignored when 'conflict' is omitted.
Extra required separation beyond touching, in map units. Default 0.
Radius around a shared endpoint of two same-layer line features within which their overlap is treated as normal end-to-end connectivity, not a conflict. Default 0 (no allowance).
Output polygon vector path with 'input_fid', 'conflict_fid', and 'overlap_area' fields. If omitted, stored in memory.

s: Spread coincident or overlapping point symbols apart to a minimum center-to-center spacing (expanded/ring/cross/square patterns) so stacked points stay individually visible, like ArcGIS Disperse Markers.

p.d: Input point vector layer.
Output point vector path (driver from extension). If omitted, stored in memory.
Minimum center-to-center spacing to enforce between clustered points, in map units.
'expanded' (default, concentric rings + local repulsion), 'ring' (single circle), 'cross' (four arms), or 'square' (grid).
Integer seed for deterministic tie-breaking when members start out exactly coincident (default 0).

s: Generate cartographic mask polygons at a margin around features (exact outline, convex hull, or bounding box), optionally clipped to a second layer (Intersecting Layers Masks).

p.d: Input vector layer (any geometry), format auto-detected (or in-memory handle).
Optional output vector path (driver from its extension). If omitted, stored in memory.
Mask margin distance. Metres for a geographic CRS (EPSG:4326 or unknown, converted to degrees), otherwise in the layer's CRS units. Must be positive.
Mask shape: 'exact' (default, buffered feature outline), 'convex_hull' (dilated convex hull), or 'box' (bounding envelope + margin).
Optional second polygon layer. When given, masks are clipped to their intersection with it (Intersecting Layers Masks); non-overlapping masks are dropped.
Optional source field whose value is copied onto each mask as 'source_id'. Defaults to the source feature index.

s: Buffer features with a choice of end-cap (round/square/butt) and corner-join (round/miter/bevel) styles, with a miter limit — the squared/mitered buffer geometry that round-only buffers cannot produce.

p.d: Input vector file path, format auto-detected (or in-memory handle).
Optional output vector path (driver from its extension). If omitted, stored in memory.
Buffer distance in the layer's CRS units. Must be positive.
End-cap style for line/point ends: 'round' (default), 'square', or 'butt' (alias 'flat').
Corner-join style: 'round' (default), 'miter', or 'bevel'.
Ratio of miter length to buffer distance beyond which a mitered corner is beveled (ArcGIS/JTS default 10). Must be >= 1. Only used when join='miter'.
When true, union all buffers into one dissolved (multi)polygon feature. Default false (one buffer per input feature, attributes preserved).

s: Build a map-series index grid of page-sized rectangles with page names (A1, B3, ... or sequential), scale-derived sizing, and an optional data-intersection filter — like ArcGIS Grid Index Features, plus a strip mode that follows a route with rotated pages like ArcGIS Strip Map Index Features.

p.d: Input vector layer. Supplies the extent when no explicit extent is given, the route for strip mode, and the features tested by intersect_only.
Output polygon vector of index pages (driver from extension). If omitted, stored in memory.
grid (default): tile a rectangular extent. strip: follow a route line with rotated overlapping pages.
Explicit extent minimum X (CRS units). Give all four of x_min/y_min/x_max/y_max to override the input extent.
Explicit extent minimum Y (CRS units).
Explicit extent maximum X (CRS units).
Explicit extent maximum Y (CRS units).
Page width in CRS units. Give both tile_width and tile_height, or use page_size + map_scale.
Page height in CRS units (page length along the route in strip mode).
Paper page preset (a0..a4, letter, legal, tabloid) whose metric dimensions are multiplied by map_scale to size each page. Requires map_scale.
Map-scale denominator (e.g. 24000 for 1:24,000). With page_size, tile size = paper metres × map_scale (metric CRS assumed).
X of the grid origin the tile boundaries align to. Default: extent minimum X.
Y of the grid origin the tile boundaries align to. Default: extent minimum Y.
Page naming scheme: alphanumeric (default; column letter + row number, e.g. A1) or sequential (reading-order number).
When true, drop pages that do not intersect any input feature. Requires input. Default false.
Strip mode: line vector layer to follow. Defaults to the first line feature in input.
Strip mode: fraction [0,1) by which consecutive pages overlap along the route. Default 0.05.
Output EPSG code when the extent is given explicitly and there is no input layer to inherit a CRS from.

s: Generate cartographic mask polygons at a margin around features of a masked layer, but only where they intersect a second masking layer (exact outline, convex hull, or bounding box).

Optional output vector path (driver from its extension). If omitted, stored in memory.

Optional field on the masked layer whose value is copied onto each mask as 'source_id'. Defaults to the source feature index.

s: Replace matched pairs of divided road lanes with single centerlines while preserving intersection connectivity, pairing only lanes that share a merge field and run anti-parallel within a separation distance, and emitting displacement polygons for propagate_displacement. Like ArcGIS Merge Divided Roads.

Field whose matching values make two lines candidate carriageway pairs (e.g. road name or class).
Maximum separation between paired carriageways, in map units.
Output merged centerline path. If omitted, stored in memory.

Optional field; features with a non-zero / non-empty value are excluded from merging.
Optional lineage table mapping output features back to their source features.

p.d: Input vector layer to adjust (any geometry type).

Displacement links: a 2-vertex line layer per link, first vertex = original location, last vertex = displaced location (the schema resolve_road_conflicts's 'links' output and rubbersheet_features's 'links' input both use).
Optional output vector path (driver from extension). If omitted, stored in memory.

'auto' (default: rigid translate for points/polygons, per-vertex bend for lines), 'preserve_orientation' (rigid translate by the field averaged over the footprint), or 'solid' (rigid translate by the field sampled once at the feature's representative point).
Maximum distance (CRS units) a link may influence a sample point; farther links are ignored. Default: unlimited (every link contributes everywhere).

s: Regularize a group of adjacent building footprints to one shared orientation so shared walls stay parallel and collinear (like ArcGIS Regularize Adjacent Building Footprint) — the group-consistent counterpart of the per-building regularize_building_footprints, which lets neighbouring footprints drift out of alignment.

p.d: Input building-footprint polygon layer.
Output polygon path. If omitted, stored in memory.
Optional field grouping footprints to regularize together. Without it, groups are formed by boundary adjacency.
'right_angles' (default) or 'right_angles_and_diagonals'.
Minimum wall length; shorter edges are pruned as noise (CRS units). Default 1.0.
Grid step for snapping wall offsets so nearby parallel walls become collinear (CRS units). Default: tolerance.
When no 'group' field is given, footprints whose vertices come within this distance are one group (CRS units). Default: 2 x tolerance.

s: Normalize noisy building footprint polygons into regular shapes (right-angle, diagonal, any-angle, or circular walls).

p.d: Input polygon vector file path, format auto-detected (or in-memory handle).
Optional output vector path (driver from its extension). If omitted, stored in memory.
Regularization method: 'right_angles' (default), 'right_angles_and_diagonals', 'any_angle', or 'circle'.
Maximum distance (in CRS units) the regularized footprint may deviate from the original boundary. Default 1.0.

For 'right_angles_and_diagonals': how strongly right angles are preferred over 45-degree walls (a wall becomes diagonal only when its angular deviation from a diagonal, times this factor, is smaller than its deviation from an axis). Default 1.5; larger values yield fewer diagonals.
For 'circle': smallest allowed fitted radius; smaller fits keep the original footprint. Default 0.1.
For 'circle': largest allowed fitted radius; larger fits keep the original footprint. Unlimited if omitted.

Image height in pixels (default: from the data aspect ratio).

Outline/line color as #rrggbb or #rrggbbaa (default dark blue).

Barrier line layer (e.g. roads) buildings must clear.
Output building layer with a 'status' field. If omitted, stored in memory.
Symbolized barrier width in map units (buffered by half this each side). Default 0.
Minimum spacing to keep between a building and a barrier (map units). Default 0.
Minimum building area (map units²) before a conflicting building is hidden rather than shrunk. Default 0 (never hide).
Whether to drop hidden buildings from the output (default false: keep them with status='hidden').

s: Displace roads whose symbolized (drawn-width) representations overlap or crowd at a target scale: lower-hierarchy roads are pushed clear of higher-hierarchy ones with endpoint-pinned, smoothed vertex shifts, optionally emitting displacement links, like ArcGIS Resolve Road Conflicts / Propagate Displacement.

p.d: Input road line layer (LineString / MultiLineString).
Output displaced road layer with 'status' and 'shift' fields. If omitted, stored in memory.
Fixed symbolized width for all roads, in map units (or page mm when 'scale' is set). Used when 'symbol_width_field' is absent.
Numeric field giving each road's symbolized width (map units, or page mm when 'scale' is set). Falls back to 'symbol_width' when a value is missing.
Numeric field ranking road importance (lower value = more important, held fixed). Absent: all roads share displacement equally.
Target map scale denominator. When set, symbol widths are page millimetres converted to ground units (mm * scale / 1000). Default: widths taken directly as map units.
Extra clear spacing to keep between symbol strips, in map units. Default 0.
Maximum displacement iterations. Default 50.
Keep the first/last vertex of every road fixed to preserve junctions/connectivity (default true).
Optional output path for displacement links (from→to lines) consumable by rubbersheet_features.

s: Reduce building footprint vertices while protecting right-angle corners, with a minimum-area drop threshold, like ArcGIS Simplify Building.

p.d: Building footprint polygons.
Optional output path. If omitted, the result is stored in memory.
Simplification tolerance in map units: the maximum distance the boundary may move.
Footprints below this area are dropped (default 0, keep all).
Emit a point at the centroid of each footprint dropped by minimum_area (default false).
Degrees within which an interior angle counts as a protected right angle (default 20).

s: Simplifies lines and polygons by replacing runs of vertices with straight segments and true circular arcs, preserving engineered curves instead of approximating them with chords (ArcGIS Simplify By Straight Lines And Circular Arcs; 'tangent' mode covers Simplify By Tangent Segments). Every simplifier in either registry is vertex-removal only, which forces a choice between a faceted curve and an unacceptable vertex count on cul-de-sac bulbs, roundabouts and tank footprints. Circles are fitted by algebraic least squares but accepted on true orthogonal deviation, so the tolerance guarantee holds.

p.d: Input line or polygon layer.
Optional output path. If omitted, the result is stored in memory.
Maximum allowed deviation of a fitted primitive from the original vertices, in CRS units.
'arcs' (default; fits straight segments and circular arcs) or 'tangent' (straight segments only, the Simplify By Tangent Segments behaviour).
Arcs subtending less than this many degrees are emitted as straight segments instead (default 10).
Arcs with a larger radius than this are emitted as straight segments (default: 1e6).
Re-densify fitted arcs to a chord tolerance on write (default true). When false only the arc endpoints are emitted, so the geometry alone loses the curve — read 'output_arcs' to recover it.
Optional path for the fitted-arc table (feature id, endpoints, centre, radius, signed sweep in degrees). If omitted, stored in memory (still returned).

s: Replaces densified curve geometry with the minimal chain of straight segments staying within a maximum perpendicular offset, joining consecutive segments at their intersection so the result remains tangent to the original (ArcGIS Simplify By Tangent Segments). The linear companion to simplify_by_circular_arcs: simplify_features (Douglas-Peucker) can only keep existing vertices and guarantees no tangency, leaving kinks on engineered geometry, while smooth_line and smooth_natural_features move vertices rather than reducing them.

p.d: Line or polygon features to simplify.
Simplified features with vertex-count fields appended. If omitted, stored in memory.

Maximum perpendicular deviation from the original, in CRS UNITS. On EPSG:4326 this is degrees, so metre-scale work needs roughly 2e-5, not 2.0. The bound is enforced against each fitted line, so the emitted chain can exceed it slightly near a joint where consecutive segments meet.
Optional point layer whose locations must survive as vertices (ArcGIS anchor_points). Runs are never grown across an anchor.
Distance within which an input vertex counts as matching an anchor point (CRS units). Default: max_offset.
Minimum number of input vertices a run must span before it is collapsed to a segment (default 3). Shorter runs are emitted unchanged.
Keep each part's first and last vertex exactly (default true).

s: Simplify a polygon coverage while keeping boundaries shared between adjacent polygons coincident (no gaps or slivers), like ArcGIS Simplify Shared Edges.

p.d: Input polygon vector file path, format auto-detected (or in-memory handle).
Optional output vector path (driver from its extension). If omitted, stored in memory.
Douglas-Peucker simplification tolerance: the maximum distance (in CRS units) a simplified arc may deviate from the original. Default 1.0.
Also simplify arcs on the coverage's outer boundary (edges belonging to a single polygon). Default true; set false to keep the outer boundary unchanged.
Quantize vertices onto a grid of this size (CRS units) before building the topology, so nearly-coincident shared vertices are treated as one. Default 0 (use coordinates exactly).

s: Smooth pixelated polygons and jagged lines (raster-to-vector outputs) into natural-looking curves via Chaikin corner cutting, preserving polygon area.

p.d: Input vector file path with polygon or line features, format auto-detected (or in-memory handle).
Optional output vector path (driver from its extension). If omitted, stored in memory.
Scale of the staircase noise to remove, in CRS units — ideally the source raster's cell size. Auto-detected from the layer's median edge length if omitted.
Chaikin smoothing iterations (1-8); more iterations give smoother output with more vertices. Default 3.
Restore each polygon's original area after smoothing (corner cutting shrinks convex shapes). Default true.

s: Smooth a polygon coverage while keeping boundaries shared between adjacent polygons coincident (no gaps or slivers), like ArcGIS Smooth Shared Edges.

p.d: Input polygon vector file path, format auto-detected (or in-memory handle).
Optional output vector path (driver from its extension). If omitted, stored in memory.
Smoothing algorithm: 'paek' (Gaussian kernel, tolerance-controlled; default) or 'bezier' (Chaikin corner-cutting, ignores tolerance).
PAEK smoothing length in CRS units: the arc-length window over which vertices are averaged. Larger values give smoother curves. Default 1.0. Ignored by the 'bezier' algorithm.
Also smooth arcs on the coverage's outer boundary (edges belonging to a single polygon). Default true; set false to keep the outer boundary unchanged.
Quantize vertices onto a grid of this size (CRS units) before building the topology, so nearly-coincident shared vertices are treated as one. Default 0 (use coordinates exactly).

Along-route length of each page, in CRS units. Required.
Cross-route width of each page, in CRS units. Required.
Fraction [0, 1) of page_length that consecutive pages overlap along the route. Default 0.
along_line (default): rotate each page to its local chord bearing. horizontal/vertical: snap rotation to the nearest east-west/north-south axis.
First page number to assign. Default 1.

Optional output vector path (driver from its extension). If omitted, stored in memory.

Optional numeric road-class field; lower value = more important (kept longer). Candidates are thinned highest-class-number first.
Name of the output visibility flag field (1 = kept, 0 = thinned). Default 'visible'.

Distance within which road endpoints are treated as the same junction. Default 1e-6.

Target attribute field compared against match_field. Defaults to match_field's name if omitted; requires match_field.

Buffer distance in map units.
Arc resolution in segments per quadrant; defaults to 8.
Line end-cap style: round, flat, or square.

p.d: Input vector layer.
Output point vector path.

Concavity ratio (default 2.0). Higher values produce a less-concave hull closer to the convex hull. Lower values allow tighter concavities.

Robustness epsilon (default 1e-9).
Output vector path.

Maximum spacing between adjacent vertices.
Output vector path.

Output layer of diced pieces. If omitted, stored in memory.

The cross-feature one-to-one matching the blind snap_endnodes lacks.

Output adjusted line layer. If omitted, stored in memory.
Maximum distance between dangling endpoints to match them.

Distance threshold for considering points coincident.
Output point vector path.

s: Fills an end-time field from the start time of the next record within each entity group, turning instant-in-time observations into time-extent records (ArcGIS Calculate End Time). transform_fields does per-value transforms and summary_statistics aggregates groups, but nothing performed a row-ordered temporal fill.

p.d: Input vector layer or table.
Timestamp field: a numeric epoch, or an ISO-8601 date/date-time string.
Field receiving the end time (default 'END_TIME'). Created if absent, overwritten if present.
Comma- or semicolon-separated grouping fields. End times are derived within a group only, never across group boundaries.
What to write for each group's final row: 'null' (default), 'same_as_start', or 'duration' (start + default_duration).
Seconds added to the start for last_record 'duration'.
Output layer. If omitted, stored in memory.

s: Annotate timestamped track points with motion statistics — speed, acceleration, bearing, segment and cumulative distance, elapsed time and idle flag — grouped by track and ordered by time, like ArcGIS Calculate Motion Statistics.

p.d: Input point vector layer of timestamped observations.
Field identifying each track/mover.
Field holding each point's time: numeric seconds or an ISO-8601 timestamp.
Output point vector (original attributes + motion fields). If omitted, stored in memory.
Trailing number of points for the smoothed 'avg_speed' (default 1 = instantaneous).
Idle radius: a point is idle when the mover travelled no more than this over the last idle_duration seconds. Default 0 (idle detection off).
Look-back window (seconds) for idle detection. Default 60.

s: Detect abrupt shifts in the time series at each location of an H3 space-time cube (like ArcGIS Change Point Detection): binary segmentation on a mean- or slope-shift cost with a sensitivity-scaled penalty (or a fixed number of change points), reporting per cell the change count, the largest change's year, and the segment means. The temporal segmentation the two-date change_vector_analysis and monotonic Mann-Kendall tests can't do.

p.d: Input point layer of timestamped events (lon/lat).
Field holding each point's time: a number or an ISO-8601 timestamp.
Output H3 polygon layer with change-point attributes. If omitted, stored in memory.
Numeric field to aggregate per bin (default: point count).
'mean' (level shifts; default) or 'slope' (trend shifts).
'auto' (penalty-based, default) or 'defined' (exactly num_change_points).
defined method: number of change points to find per location (default 1).
auto method: penalty scale; higher = fewer change points (default 1.0).
Width of a time step in the time_field's units (default 1).
H3 resolution 0..15 (default 7).

s: Flag where a condition starts and ends along each track: group timestamped points by track, sort by time, evaluate a start (and optional end) comparison over a numeric attribute, and emit incident episodes as flagged points or per-episode line segments with ids and durations — like ArcGIS Detect Incidents.

p.d: Input point vector layer of timestamped observations.
Field identifying each track/mover (e.g. vehicle or animal id).
Field holding each point's time: numeric seconds or an ISO-8601 timestamp.
Condition that opens an incident, e.g. 'speed > 30'. Grammar: '<field> <op> <number>' with op one of > >= < <= == != , optionally two clauses joined by AND.
Optional condition that closes an incident (same grammar). If omitted, an incident ends when the start condition stops holding.
Output mode: 'points' (default, every point copied through with incident fields) or 'segments' (one polyline per incident).
Output vector path (driver from extension). If omitted, stored in memory.

s: Space-time hot spot trends on an H3 space-time cube: bin timestamped points into H3 cells x time steps, compute Getis-Ord Gi* per bin, and classify each cell (new/intensifying/persistent/diminishing/... hot or cold spot) via a Mann-Kendall trend test, like ArcGIS Emerging Hot Spot Analysis.

p.d: Input point vector layer (geographic lon/lat, EPSG:4326). Other geometries use their vertex-mean representative point.
Output vector path (driver from extension). One H3 polygon per cell. If omitted, stored in memory.
Field holding each point's time: a numeric field (its own units) or an ISO-8601 date/datetime string.
Width of a time step: a plain number (numeric time_field) or a duration like '1w', '7d', '12h', '1M' for a date field. Default '1w'.
Optional numeric field summed into each bin. Default: count of points per bin.
H3 resolution 0 (coarsest) to 15 (finest); default 7 (~5 km² cells).
Spatial neighborhood radius in H3 k-rings (default 1).
Temporal neighborhood radius in time steps (default 1).

s: Detect where a moving entity stayed put: runs of track fixes within a distance tolerance for at least a time tolerance, emitted as fixes, mean centers or convex hulls, like ArcGIS Find Dwell Locations.

Field identifying the track each fix belongs to.
Timestamp field (numeric seconds or ISO-8601 text).
Optional output path. If omitted, the result is stored in memory.
Maximum distance (map units) a fix may sit from the dwell's running centroid.
Minimum duration (same units as time_field) for a stationary run to count as a dwell.
dwell_features (default) | mean_centers | convex_hulls | all_features.

Emits area hulls and representative points with participant count, start/end time, and duration.

p.d: Timestamped track point layer (projected CRS; distances in map units).
Field identifying each track/entity.
Field holding each point's time: numeric seconds or an ISO-8601 timestamp.
Maximum distance (map units) for tracks to count as together.
Minimum duration (time units) a gathering must persist to be reported.
Optional maximum duration; longer gatherings are dropped.
Minimum number of distinct tracks in a gathering (default 2).
Width of a time slice (time units). Default: min_meeting_duration.
Output representative-point layer (one point per meeting). If omitted, stored in memory.
Optional output area layer (convex-hull polygon per meeting). If omitted, stored in memory.

Secondary point layer to match against.

Output match layer (one link line per matched pair). If omitted, stored in memory.
Maximum spatial distance between a primary and secondary feature (map units).
Maximum time separation: a number of seconds or a duration like '2h', '30m', '7d'.
'either' (default), 'before' (secondary before primary), or 'after' (secondary after primary).
Field naming each primary feature in the output (default: feature index).
Field naming each secondary feature in the output (default: feature index).

Maximum tree depth (default 8).
Seed for the deterministic RNG driving bootstrapping and feature subsetting (default 42).

Width of a time step in the time_field's units (default 1).
H3 resolution 0..15 (default 7).
Spatial neighbourhood k-ring radius (default 1).
Temporal neighbourhood half-width in steps (default 1).
Permutations for the significance test (default 99; 0 disables).
Seed for the permutation RNG (default 1).

Attribute that partitions points into separate paths (one line per distinct value). If omitted, all points form a single path.

Append the first vertex to the end of each path, closing it into a ring. Default false.

Field identifying each track/mover (e.g. vehicle or animal id).
Field holding each point's time: numeric seconds or an ISO-8601 timestamp.

Start a new track segment when the time gap between points exceeds this many seconds. Default: no time split.
Start a new track segment when the distance between points exceeds this (metres for geographic CRS, CRS units otherwise). Default: no distance split.

Timestamp field (numeric or ISO-8601 date/datetime).

Time-series distance: 'value' (raw), 'profile' (z-normalized, default), or 'correlation' (1 − r).

Optional numeric field summed into each bin. Default: count of points per bin.
H3 resolution 0 (coarsest) to 15 (finest); default 7 (~5 km² cells).
Random seed for reproducible medoid initialization (default 1).

p.d: Input point layer of timestamped events (lon/lat).
Field holding each point's time: a number or an ISO-8601 timestamp.
Output H3 polygon layer with forecast attributes. If omitted, stored in memory.
Numeric field to aggregate per bin (default: point count).
Number of time steps to forecast ahead (default 3).
'auto' (lowest hold-out RMSE; default), 'exp_smoothing', 'linear', or 'parabolic'.

Numeric field whose series is smoothed.

Target polygons to predict values for.
Numeric value field on the source polygons.

Approximate number of interior points used to represent each polygon's area support (default 25). Higher is more accurate and much slower.
Variogram model: 'exponential' (default), 'spherical', or 'gaussian'.

Rescale count predictions so the target total matches the source total (default true for 'count', always off for 'average'). Only applied when the targets cover the sources — the applied factor is reported as 'mass_scale' so a partial-coverage run is visible.

Numeric field with the lower bound of the value. Use together with upper_field instead of error_field.
Numeric field with the upper bound of the value. Use together with lower_field instead of error_field.

Seed for the deterministic RNG (default 1).
Output vector layer with the appended statistics. If omitted, stored in memory.

First numeric variable field.
Second numeric variable field.
Output layer with local L, p-value, and class fields. If omitted, stored in memory.

Number of permutations for the significance test (default 199; 0 disables).
Seed for the permutation RNG (default 1), for reproducible results.

Neighbour count k (>= 1). Default 1.
'euclidean' (default) or 'manhattan'.
Optional CSV path for a feature_id,kth_neighbor_distance table.

Field holding the event count (numerator).
Field holding the population at risk (denominator).
Output layer with rate fields added. If omitted, stored in memory.
'crude', 'eb_global' (default), or 'eb_spatial'.
Rate multiplier, e.g. 100000 for per-100k (default 100000).
eb_spatial only: number of nearest neighbours for the local reference rate (default 8).

Numeric outcome (dependent) field.

Comma-separated numeric confounder field(s) to adjust for.

If true, widen the confounder set with each feature's x/y coordinates plus the k-nearest-neighbour average of each confounder (default false).
Standardized-mean-difference threshold for the post-adjustment balance check (default 0.1).
Optional output vector path (input copy + propensity score / weight / match-id columns). If omitted, stored in memory.
Integer seed for the deterministic bootstrap confidence interval (default 42).

Output vector path (driver from extension). If omitted, stored in memory.
'central_feature' (default) or 'linear_directional_mean'.
Optional numeric field weighting each feature (central_feature only).
Optional field to group features by; one result per distinct value.
Distance metric for central_feature: 'euclidean' (default) or 'manhattan'.
Treat lines as undirected (orientation mod 180°) for linear_directional_mean. Default false.

s: Collapse coincident incident points into unique locations, each carrying an ICOUNT count of the events there, like ArcGIS Collect Events.

s: Rank candidate features by attribute similarity to one or more reference features across z-standardized numeric fields (Euclidean or cosine), most/least/both — like ArcGIS Similarity Search.

p.d: Reference vector layer (one or more features defining the profile to match).
Candidate vector layer to rank by similarity to the reference.

s: Generate Moran eigenvectors (spatial filters) from a spatial weights matrix and append the autocorrelated components as explanatory-variable fields (MEV1, MEV2, …), like ArcGIS Decompose Spatial Structure / Create Spatial Component Explanatory Variables. Builds a symmetric connectivity matrix (contiguity or symmetrized KNN), double-centres it (M C M), and eigendecomposes it with a pure-Rust cyclic-Jacobi solver; keeps eigenvectors whose Moran's I ≥ min_autocorrelation, ranked descending and capped at max_components.

p.d: Input vector layer (points/lines/polygons; contiguity methods require polygons).
Output vector path — the input features with the kept eigenvectors appended as MEV1, MEV2, …. If omitted, stored in memory.
Conceptualization of spatial relationships: 'contiguity_edges' (rook), 'contiguity_edges_corners' (queen), or 'knn' (symmetrized). Default 'contiguity_edges_corners'.
Number of nearest neighbours k for method = knn. Default 8.
Minimum Moran's I an eigenvector must have to be kept (positive spatial autocorrelation). Default 0.25.
Maximum number of eigenvectors to emit, taken in descending Moran's I order. Default 15.

s: Score points by their Local Outlier Factor (LOF) — how isolated each point is relative to the local density of its k nearest neighbours — and flag the top outliers, like ArcGIS Spatial Outlier Detection. Fills the gap DBSCAN's binary noise label leaves.

p.d: Input point vector layer.
Output points with LOF score and outlier flag. If omitted, stored in memory.
Number of nearest neighbours k (default 20).
Flag the top this-percent of points by LOF as outliers (default 5). Ignored if 'threshold' is set.
Explicit LOF cutoff: points with LOF above this are outliers (overrides percent_outlier).

s: Partition features into spatially contiguous, attribute-homogeneous regions with the SKATER algorithm (minimum spanning tree over a contiguity graph, cut to maximise between-cluster variance), with optional size/balance constraints. Every cluster is connected by construction, unlike multivariate_clustering. Like ArcGIS Spatially Constrained Multivariate Clustering.

p.d: Input polygon (or point) features.
Output path for the input features plus a CLUSTER_ID field. If omitted, stored in memory.
Comma/semicolon-separated numeric field names to cluster on.
Target number of clusters (default 5).
'contiguity_edges' (rook, default), 'contiguity_edges_corners' (queen) or 'knn'.
Neighbour count for the 'knn' neighbourhood (default 8).
'none' (default), 'feature_count' or 'attribute_value'.
Field summed per cluster when 'constraint' is 'attribute_value'.
Minimum per-cluster feature count or attribute total; cuts violating it are skipped.
Maximum per-cluster feature count or attribute total; clusters above it are split further even past 'number_of_clusters'.
